recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中的顆粒球核只有兩葉，呈對稱的圓形或啞鈴狀「夾鼻眼鏡（pince-nez）」外觀，染色質粗糙緊密，細胞質顆粒正常、沒有發育不良的其他表現；另見單一圓核的顆粒球。在家族史背景下符合 Pelger–Huët anomaly。
features: Mature-sized granulocytes with bilobed nuclei forming symmetric round lobes (pince-nez/spectacle configuration)
Markedly coarse, condensed chromatin indicating nuclear maturity despite hyposegmentation
Normal cytoplasmic granulation without hypogranularity or vacuolation
One granulocyte with a single round, non-segmented nucleus (Stodtmeister-type form; low magnification, cell type uncertain)
Background red cells and platelets unremarkable; a smudged/disrupted leukocyte is present
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells without significant poikilocytosis and adequate, normal-appearing platelets. Granulocytes display nuclear hyposegmentation, with bilobed nuclei composed of two symmetric, rounded lobes in a pince-nez configuration, and a granulocyte with a single round nucleus is also seen at low power. The chromatin is coarse and clumped, and cytoplasmic granulation is normal, without dysgranulopoiesis. In an otherwise healthy infant with affected family members, the findings are consistent with Pelger–Huët anomaly.

ddx.vs: Acquired pseudo-Pelger cells typically affect only a subset of neutrophils and are accompanied by hypogranular cytoplasm, cytopenias and other dysplasia, whereas inherited PHA involves nearly all neutrophils with normal granulation and no cytopenias.

ddx.dx: Drug-induced pseudo-Pelger change (e.g., mycophenolate, colchicine, taxanes, valproate)
ddx.vs: Drug effect is transient and linked to exposure, while PHA is lifelong and familial, which requires history and family smears rather than morphology alone.
Bands have a C- or U-shaped unsegmented nucleus with less condensed chromatin, whereas Pelger cells have round, dense, fully mature lobes.
SGD also shows bilobed nuclei but with markedly reduced secondary granules and recurrent infections, unlike the normally granulated cells here.
